description: 🌙 Lunar Minds is a team passionate about AI, Data Science, software, and space exploration. We're taking on NASA's “Flame in Freefall” challenge to build an AI-powered platform for exploring microgravity combustion research and fire-safety insights. 🚀 We're looking for teammates skilled in AI/ML, Python, Data Science, Web Development, UI/UX, Statistics, Space Science, or Research. 🌎 Open to participants worldwide!
summary:
FIREWISE AI is an AI-powered Space Fire Research Assistant designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand.

The platform uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Google's Gemini AI to retrieve information from NASA research documents and generate context-aware answers with source citations.

Its key features include a NASA research library, AI research assistant, PDF document analysis, experiment insights, and research report generation.

Focusing on spacecraft fire research, microgravity combustion, flame spread, and material flammability, FIREWISE AI helps students and researchers access complex scientific information more efficiently.

The project aims to support space science education and research by making NASA's combustion research more accessible through artificial intelligence. It is an educational research tool, not a certified spacecraft fire prediction or safety system.
details:
1. Project Overview

FIREWISE AI is an AI-powered Space Fire Research Assistant designed to make NASA's microgravity combustion research easier to explore, understand and access. It combines artificial intelligence with scientific research resources to help students, researchers and space science enthusiasts investigate spacecraft fire-related research.

2. How It Works

FIREWISE AI uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with Google's Gemini AI model.

The system retrieves relevant information from its indexed research document and uses that context to generate AI-assisted answers with supporting citations.

Its main features include:

  • NASA Research Library: Explore selected NASA combustion research resources.
  • AI Research Assistant: Ask questions about space fire research and receive context-aware answers with citations.
  • PDF Analysis: Upload research PDFs and extract relevant scientific information.
  • Experiment Insights: Explore research topics involving microgravity combustion, flame spread and material flammability.
  • Research Reports: Generate downloadable reports from research information.

3. Technology Used

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, Vite and CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • AI Model: Google Gemini API.
  • Research Architecture: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Document Processing: PDF text extraction.
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code and GitHub.

4. NASA Research Resources

The project references NASA research involving BASS-II, SAFFIRE and FLEX experiments. The BASS-II PMMA combustion research document is currently indexed for RAG-based question answering. Other NASA research resources are included in the research catalogue.

5. Innovation and Intended Impact

FIREWISE AI combines scientific research with generative AI to make complex space combustion information easier to explore. It provides an accessible research interface, helps users locate supporting sources and reduces the effort required to navigate technical research documents.

The project aims to support space science education and encourage further exploration of spacecraft fire safety research.

6. Limitations and Safety Considerations

FIREWISE AI is an educational and research-support platform. Its AI-generated responses may contain errors and should be checked against the original research documents. It is not a validated fire prediction model, certified spacecraft fire simulator or operational spacecraft safety system.
